_comment: Mostly hand-maintained; `verifiedViaProxy` is generated from a real `npm run test:proxy` run by `npm run proxy:status -- --write` and checked against that run (it fails if the two disagree). Add an entry here when a lab's automated tests + manual verification are actually done — the coverage matrix script (scripts/print-coverage-matrix.ts) will otherwise show that lab as implemented-but-unverified rather than assuming it's covered.

Negative cases: direct visit to the real page (no click) and the decoy page WITHOUT the iframe both confirmed NOT to solve it. Generic contract: tests/integration/lab-contract.test.ts.

mp-prototype-pollution-admin.note: Purely client-side vulnerability; exploit verified via the REAL headless-browser admin-bot (the JS actually runs), including a baseline visit with a harmless payload that confirms isAdmin() stays false. Generic contract: tests/integration/lab-contract.test.ts.

mc-host-header-reset-poisoning.note: Exploit + negative case driven with node:http directly (not fetch — the Fetch spec forbids scripts from setting the Host header, same as a real browser), which is the only way to genuinely forge it outside a proxy like Burp. Generic contract: tests/integration/lab-contract.test.ts.

xp-svg-upload-stored-xss.note: Exploit + negative case (a harmless SVG) driven through the real headless-browser admin-bot; first implementation used <object> embedding, which creates an isolated nested document the payload couldn't escape — caught by the test, fixed by inlining the SVG's raw markup into the page instead, which is also the more realistic real-world vector. Generic contract: tests/integration/lab-contract.test.ts.
